summary.text: Saint Nikodemos was an Athonite monk and editor whose work transmitted patristic, liturgical, and canonical texts, including the Philokalia and the Rudder.

blocks.text: The OCA dates his birth on Naxos to 1748 and gives Nicholas as his baptismal name. He studied there, entered Dionysiou Monastery on Mount Athos, and received the monastic name Nikodemos.

blocks.text: He first worked as the monastery’s secretary. Saint Makarios of Corinth entrusted him with editing the Philokalia manuscript. Later he combined further monastic formation with extensive editorial work, including preparing writings by earlier Orthodox teachers.

blocks.text: In declining health he stayed with two brother iconographers, who helped him. He received the Church’s sacraments before his peaceful death on July 14, 1809. Constantinople formally glorified him in 1955; he was not a martyr.

blocks.text: His publications include a confession manual, liturgical canons, Saints’ lives, and the Rudder, a collection of Church canons prepared with a collaborator. These are different genres: pastoral counsel, hymnography, hagiography, and canon law.
